examples.en: I fell and my ribs hurt.
The doctor checked my ribs.

examples.ko: 갈비뼈는 가슴 속 장기를 지켜 줘요.
examples.en: The ribs protect the organs inside the chest.
My rib area hurt, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 갈비뼈에 금이 가서 한 달 동안 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I cracked a rib and rested for a month.
I had an X-ray taken to see whether the ribs were hurt too.

explain: '갈비'는 먹는 고기 이름으로 더 잘 알려져 있어요. 몸 안의 뼈를 말할 때는 '갈비뼈'라고 하고, 다쳤을 때는 '갈비뼈에 금이 가다', '갈비뼈가 부러지다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: '갈비' is better known as a cut of meat to eat. For the bone in the body, say '갈비뼈'. When injured: '갈비뼈에 금이 가다' (crack a rib), '갈비뼈가 부러지다' (break a rib).

examples.en: I stepped in dog droppings on the street and my shoes got dirty.
You put dog droppings in a bag and throw them in the trash.
There was a lot of dog mess in the park, so I walked carefully.

examples.ko: 창문을 열었더니 개똥 냄새가 나서 닫았어요.
examples.en: I opened the window, smelled dog droppings, and closed it.
I almost slipped on dog droppings without noticing.
A puppy left dog droppings in the park.

explain: '소똥', '말똥'처럼 동물 이름 뒤에 '똥'을 붙여요. 사람이 눈 것은 그냥 '똥'이라고 해요. 똥은 거친 말은 아니지만 밥 먹을 때 꺼내기는 조심해요.

phrases.example: 평소에는 흔하던 우산이 비 오는 날엔 하나도 안 보여요. 개똥도 약에 쓰려면 없다더니 그 말이 맞네요.
phrases.en: Even dog dung is nowhere to be found when you need it as medicine
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소에 흔하던 것도 막상 필요해서 찾으면 없을 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb for when something that was everywhere suddenly cannot be found once you need it.
phrases.en_equiv: You can never find it when you need it.

explain_en: Animal droppings are named by putting the animal first, like '소똥' and '말똥'. A person's is just '똥'. It is not rude, but people avoid bringing it up while eating.

examples.en: I am sorry, I forgot our appointment.
I forgot my umbrella and just came out.
I forgot where I put my keys.
I will write a note so I do not forget again.
I have been forgetting things more lately.
Sometimes I forget my password.

explain: '잊어버리다'보다 가볍게, 잠깐 놓쳤다는 느낌으로 써요. '깜빡 잊었어요', '깜빡했어요' 둘 다 말해요. 눈을 '깜빡이다'와 소리가 비슷하지만 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: It feels lighter than 'ijeobeorida': you just missed it for a moment. People say both 'kkamppak ijeosseoyo' and 'kkamppakaesseoyo'. It sounds close to 'kkamppagida' (to blink) but means something different.

examples.en: I bought new basketball shoes last week.

examples.ko: 이 농구화는 발목을 잘 잡아 줘요.
examples.en: These basketball shoes support your ankles well.
My basketball shoe lace came undone, so I tied it again.
You have to wear basketball shoes in the gym.

examples.ko: 형은 농구화를 아껴서 늘 깨끗이 닦아요.
examples.en: My older brother takes care of his basketball shoes and always cleans them.

examples.ko: 농구화가 커서 양말을 두 켤레 신어요.
examples.en: The basketball shoes are big, so I wear two pairs of socks.

explain: 운동할 때 신는 신발 이름에는 축구화, 러닝화, 등산화처럼 종목 이름을 붙여요. 신발을 세는 말은 '켤레'예요. 신발은 '신다'를 써서 '농구화를 신다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Shoes for sports are named by adding the sport, as in 축구화, 러닝화 and 등산화. The counter for shoes is '켤레'. You wear shoes with '신다', so it is '농구화를 신다'.

examples.en: I held my bangs in place with a small hairpin.
I bought a pretty hairpin at a gift shop.
My hairpin keeps falling out, so it's annoying.
I pinned my bangs up with two hairpins.
How much is that red hairpin over there?
Please wrap the hairpin I'm giving to my younger sibling.

explain: 머리핀은 보통 '꽂다'를 쓰고, 끈으로 묶는 '머리끈'은 '묶다'를 써서 동사가 달라요. 머리에 하는 것은 '머리핀을 꽂다', '머리띠를 하다'처럼 말해요. 영어식으로 '헤어핀'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: For a hairpin you usually use the verb '꽂다', while for a hair tie '머리끈' you use '묶다', so the verbs differ. Things worn in the hair go with different verbs, as in '머리핀을 꽂다' and '머리띠를 하다'. It is also called '헤어핀', the English-style word.

examples.en: I often skip my homework.
I forgot to write my name on the test paper.
I have no plans to skip class.
I want to fix my habit of skipping medicine.
I skipped the explanation and solved the problem right away.
I left out one line, so points were deducted.

explain: 일부러 안 할 때도, 깜빡해서 못 할 때도 써요. 중립적으로 말하면 '빠뜨리다'가 무난하고, '빼먹다'는 말투가 편해요. 수업, 숙제, 식사 같은 말과 자주 어울려요.
explain_en: It covers both skipping on purpose and missing something by accident. The neutral choice is '빠뜨리다'; '빼먹다' is more casual. It often goes with class, homework, and meals.

en: to delete; to remove; to eliminate

examples.en: I delete photos I don't need every day.
I deleted an important email by mistake.
You must not delete this file.
I deleted the app and installed it again.
To delete a message, press and hold it.

examples.ko: 삭제한 사진은 휴지통에서 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can find deleted photos in the trash.

explain: 손으로 쓴 글씨나 연필 자국은 '지우다'이고, 컴퓨터·휴대폰의 파일·사진·메시지는 '삭제하다'를 많이 써요. 말할 때는 '사진 지웠어요'도 자주 해요. 삭제한 걸 되살리는 건 '복구하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Handwriting and pencil marks are '지우다' (erase), while files, photos and messages on a computer or phone are usually 삭제하다. In speech people also say '사진 지웠어요'. Bringing back something you deleted is '복구하다'.

examples.ko: 영화 보면서 스낵을 한 봉지 다 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate a whole bag of snacks while watching a movie.

examples.ko: 실례지만 이 마트의 스낵 코너가 어디예요?
examples.en: Excuse me, where is the snack section of this mart?
At the picnic I handed out snacks to the children.

examples.ko: 이 스낵은 맛은 좋은데 너무 짜요.
examples.en: This snack tastes good but is too salty.

examples.ko: 스낵 한 봉지를 사서 나눠 먹었어요.
examples.en: I bought a bag of snacks and we shared it.
There are so many kinds of snacks that it's hard to choose.

explain: 한국어에서 봉지에 든 간식은 대부분 '과자'라고 해요. '스낵'은 포장지나 마트 코너 이름에서 자주 보이지만, 말할 때는 '과자 사 올게'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 스낵 종류를 말할 때는 '스낵류'라고도 써요.
explain_en: In Korean, packaged snacks are mostly just called 과자. 스낵 appears often on packages and store sections, but in speech '과자 사 올게' (I'll go buy snacks) is far more natural. You may also see '스낵류' (snack category) in labels.

p.n: 과자 is the everyday native-feeling word; 스낵 sounds like a product category.

examples.en: If there is cold rice, I make fried rice.
I heat cold rice in the microwave before eating.
I ate the leftover cold rice from the morning for lunch.
I made porridge with cold rice.

examples.ko: 찬밥이 싫으면 따뜻한 밥을 새로 지을게요.
examples.en: If you do not like cold rice, I will cook fresh rice.

examples.ko: 냄비에 찬밥 한 공기가 남아 있어요.
examples.en: There is a bowl of cold rice left in the pot.

explain: '식은 밥'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 반대는 '따뜻한 밥'이나 '더운밥'이에요. 식은 밥으로 볶음밥이나 죽을 많이 만들어요.

phrases.example: 새 직원이 들어오자 그는 찬밥 신세가 됐어요.
phrases.en: When a new employee joined, he was left out in the cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸모없다고 여겨져 푸대접을 받는 처지를 말해요. 주로 불만이나 서운함을 담아 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone treated as useless and neglected. It usually carries a tone of complaint or hurt.
phrases.en_equiv: be left out in the cold

explain_en: It means almost the same as '식은 밥', and the opposite is '따뜻한 밥' or '더운밥'. Cold rice is often used to make fried rice or porridge.

examples.en: The mussel broth is really refreshing.
I added mussels and boiled a soup.
You have to wash mussel shells clean.

examples.ko: 홍합이 입을 벌리면 다 익은 거예요.
examples.en: When the mussels open their shells, they are done.
I added mussels and clams together.
I made the jjamppong broth with mussels.

explain: 검은색 긴 껍데기를 가진 조개류예요. 국물 맛이 시원해서 탕이나 짬뽕에 많이 넣어요. 보통 '조개'와는 모양이 달라서 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It is a shellfish with a long dark shell. Its broth tastes clean and refreshing, so it is often added to soups and jjamppong. Its shape differs from typical '조개' (clams), so it has its own name.
